current.text: Toronto traded Brandon Ingram and added Kawhi Leonard.
He is a projected starter next to Quickley, Leonard, Barnes and Poeltl. He is also in the expected closing five.
The Raptors have 15 back-to-backs this season and three in the fantasy playoffs.
Experts see him as the biggest loser of the Kawhi trade. Usage moves to Kawhi, so Barrett will have the ball less.
He should still start and play 30 or more minutes. Kawhi Leonard's load management helps him, and he should step up in the games Kawhi misses.
Sean expects his finishing next to Kawhi and Scottie Barnes to reach impressive levels this season.
Because of his contract, he could become a trade candidate by the deadline if the season starts badly.
Experts differ on his category price. One ranks him tier seven among small forwards and outside the top 130 in category leagues, and calls a Yahoo ADP of 107 too high. Josh is very okay drafting him.

durable.text: He is mainly a scorer. His defense is limited, his steals and blocks are low, and his efficiency is lower.
He is worth clearly more in points leagues than in category leagues.
His FT% is a clear weakness. He shoots below 70% on close to 5 attempts per game, which hurts a team's FT%.

note: He is a late-auction player for us: Yahoo and ESPN both price him near 1 USD (ranks 124 and 140), and he went for 1 USD in our league last season. In 9-cat his value comes from points and some rebounds. His FT% around 69% on real volume and his low steals and blocks hold him back, so he only makes sense as a cheap scorer late in the draft. Early in the season, check how much usage he keeps next to Kawhi and whether he produces more in the games Kawhi rests.
